First Light: The kettle clicks, the room turns gold
A bicycle rolls down the road
You draw a sun against the glass
And let the quiet morning pass
First light across the kitchen floor
A little less to hurry for
The day can wait outside the door
The rooftops shake their shadows loose
I leave the last warm cup for you
We make no promise to the day
Just open up and let it stay
Paper Planes: I fold the corners of a map
And send a small blue country back
Across the table, past your hand
To somewhere neither of us planned
Room for all the unmade things
One takes the window for the sky
You catch the last before it falls
And draw a doorway on the wall
Soft Geometry: Your coat makes mountains on the chair
A crooked line across the room
Round the edges of the day
Let the hard lines fall away
Leave a little space beside me
The window holds a square of blue
The shadows find a shape that's new
We move the table to the sun
Slow Motion: A drop of rain forgets to fall
The clock leans softly on the wall
Your hand is halfway to the door
I ask for nothing, then for more
The whole world waiting in this room
A second opens like a mile
And lets us stay a little while
The traffic hums below the sill
The cup between us holds its warmth
We watch a shadow leave the hill
And let the next small moment form
Blue Hour: The last train leaves a silver line
Across the water, out of sight
We take the long way by the shore
Blue hour, keep the city low
Between the daylight and the dark
I know this quiet place by heart
Your footsteps find a slower beat
The river gathers all the streets
A boat moves underneath the bridge
And takes the little light with it
Night Current: The ferry leaves at half past ten
Its yellow windows turn the bend
I watch the wake divide the stars
And carry them away from ours
Past the places I can see
Leave a ribbon on the bay
For the things I couldn't say
A bell rings somewhere down the quay
The sound comes slowly back to me
The shore is only points of light
Enough to find our way tonight
City in Rain: An empty bus, a corner shop
A red light asking us to stop
Let the city turn to rain
Every street we thought we knew
We count the steps beneath the eaves
A doorway gives us somewhere dry
We wait and watch the weather by
Distant Windows: A lamp comes on across the street
A curtain lifts, a shadow bends
A small square of the evening ends
Little rooms that hold the night
I leave a light where you can see
One more window, here with me
We never need to know their names
To share the warmth behind the panes
Golden Hours: We missed the turning for the coast
And found the road we needed most
Your shadow stretching down the wall
Leave the long way home to find
Keep a little of the sun
For the days still yet to come
The dust is dancing in the lane
You say we'll pass this way again
Inside the words I didn't say
Small Adventures: We took the bus two stops too far
And found a garden through the bars
A dog asleep beneath a chair
A place we'd never thought was there
A little less of keeping score
We bought two peaches for the walk
And let the road do half the talk
No postcard waiting to be sent
Just being glad of where we went
Sunroom: The plants are leaning toward the glass
A bee is waiting for a gap
You turn the pages of a book
I like the way the silence looks
Let the garden climb the wall
We have nowhere else at all
A cloud puts shade across your knee
You lift your eyes and look at me
The bee has found the open door
The light comes back across the floor
The Way Home: The market closes one stall late
We stop beside the railway gate
You know a path behind the school
Where evening makes the garden cool
The way home isn't always straight
There is a little room for late
Follow where the warm lights go
The road remembers what we know
A neighbour waves and calls your name
The houses look almost the same
Then there's the step, the turning key
The place that kept a space for me
Quiet Orbit: A cup goes cold beside the bed
You draw a circle with your thumb
Around the place I'm speaking from
Far enough to see the whole
Near enough to still be home
The ceiling slowly fills with blue
There is no distance here to prove
We let the planet turn below
And watch the slow blue morning grow
Weightless: I put my keys beside the door
And leave the day there on the floor
The room is floating out of reach
Let the ceiling be the sky
You turn the music down a shade
The sofa holds the shapes we made
I lose the edges of the week
And find the room enough to breathe
Open Skies: The hills are wearing evening fire
We leave the car beside the lane
And let the wind decide our names
All the room we need is here
The grass is taller than before
A bird is heading for the shore
And listen with our open ears
Goodnight, Satellite: A little light above the trees
Goes round the world while no one sees
I watch it cross the window frame
And give it your familiar name
Keep a circle in the night
When the morning finds this place
The room is quiet, almost still
The moon has climbed the windowsill
Tomorrow has a while to go
I turn the lamp down soft and low
